new.headline: You ran this week exactly as planned, and with the race moved to Oct 18 the 22-miler is off. Sunday's 16 miles with 6 at goal pace is your last long run before a two-week taper.

answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, drop the 22-miler. With the race on Sun Oct 18, there isn't enough time to run it and recover before the start.

At your long-run pace, 22 miles would take about 3 hours 40 minutes. Beyond about 3 hours, extra time on your feet adds more tiredness than fitness. A run that long can take two weeks or more to recover from, so you'd still be carrying it on race day.

One 20 is enough. Since then you've run a 15 and a 17 on steady 40-mile weeks, and the 17 had almost no heart-rate drift. You've already built that endurance, and it won't fade in three weeks.

Running marathon pace on tired legs will help you more now. Next Sunday's 16 miles with 6 at goal pace is your last long run, and then the taper does the work.

new.analysis:
**You ran this week exactly as written.** Every run matched its planned distance, and the threshold reps held pace with almost no slowdown. That matters after Sep 7 – 13, when the week grew to 53 miles and a planned 15 became a 20.

| Day | Planned | What you ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tue Sep 22 | 6 mi easy | 6.0 mi at 9:52/mi, HR 138 |
| Wed Sep 23 | 9 mi with 3 x 2 mi threshold | 9.0 mi, reps at 7:58/mi, 1% fade |
| Thu Sep 24 | 6 mi easy | 6.0 mi at 9:51/mi, HR 139 |
| Sat Sep 26 | 4 mi easy | 4.0 mi at 9:54/mi, HR 138 |
| Sun Sep 27 | 17 mi long | 17.0 mi at 9:59/mi, HR 146 |

**Your fitness is steady and on track for the target.** Easy runs held 9:50/mi at 138 bpm, the same as three weeks ago. Your heart rate rose less than 5 bpm over the 17-miler. Threshold reps near 8:00/mi and the Sep 16 goal-pace miles near 8:35/mi both fit a sub-3:45 race.

**A 61% easy share is fine for a week like this.** A threshold session plus a long run that sits between zones 2 and 3 pulls that number into the 60s. Your easy days were 97% zone 2, and that's the number that counts.

**The new race date sets the shape of next week.** This is the last full week, so mileage holds at about 40 with two hard days kept apart by easy ones. The threshold work is a little shorter so Sunday's goal-pace miles start on fresh legs.

**The taper starts right after Sunday.** Expect about 30 miles for Oct 5 – 11 with a shorter long run, then a light race week. Keep your two strength sessions next week but use lighter weights, and stop heavy lifting about ten days before the race.

**Feeling anxious about the new date is normal, and it doesn't change your fitness.** You lose two weeks of build, but the most important work is already done. You'll race on the last six weeks of training, not on one more long run.
